title: The Dimple factor: Can she crack BJP's women-voter fortress & deliver UP to Akhilesh?
content: Dimple Yadav is stepping into the spotlight with a heightened political presence within the Samajwadi Party. As she actively campaigns and addresses rallies in anticipation of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, her efforts aim to connect with women voters—a key demographic for the party's triumph. Her initiatives are centered on empowering women and addressing social issues that speak to the electorate.

title: Manipur in turmoil again: 15 houses torched; 1 killed, several injured in gun attack
content: In Chassad village, located in Manipur's Kamjong district, at least 15 houses were burned late Saturday night. Suspected militants attacked the village, causing significant chaos and civilians to flee for safety. A Kuki civilian was killed during the assault, and four others suffered injuries from gunfire. Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence and called for strict action against the perpetrators.

title: Narrow space, single gate: Home guards’ role under lens in Kolkata stampede; 7 remanded
content: Suvendu Adhikari has ordered an investigation into the stampede at Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal that resulted in 19 deaths. The crowded conditions worsened by rain contributed significantly to the tragic event. Adhikari criticized the previous TMC administration for leaving behind issues that led to this disaster. Additionally, seven individuals connected to the incident have been remanded to police custody for further questioning.

title: Michael Dell pledges $6.25bn to Trump Accounts after giving $750m to UT Austin
content: Michael Dell and Susan Dell are the biggest private donors to Trump Accounts, with a $6.25 billion pledge putting $250 into the investment accounts of 25 million American children. Before this, their home state of Texas was the main focus of their philanthropy. In April, the couple committed $750 million to UT Austin for a new AI-native medical campus, becoming the university's first billion-dollar donors.

title: Texas Supreme Court to decide if city can take $1.1m property for golf facility
content: The Texas Supreme Court will examine an eminent domain case involving Westworth Village's attempt to acquire land from Jim Burgess for a golf facility. Following a previous ruling that deemed the taking unconstitutional on public use grounds, the case delves into the legality of local governments appropriating private property for private enterprise projects. This decision holds the potential to set a major precedent for eminent domain laws throughout Texas.

title: France's unrest spills across borders as protests turn violent in Belgium, Italy
content: France is witnessing explosive protests over soaring living expenses and inadequate public services, sparking clashes with police forces. This unrest has spilled over into neighboring Belgium and Italy, marking a significant uptick in regional tensions. With more than 500 police officers reported injured and severe property destruction across various cities, officials in both Belgium and Italy have condemned the clashes while understanding the underlying issues.

title: Brendan Taylor surpasses Andy Flower to become Zimbabwe’s highest ODI run-scorer
content: In a remarkable feat, Brendan Taylor eclipsed Andy Flower as Zimbabwe's leading ODI run-scorer by scoring 81 runs during a match against Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. This stellar performance not only played a pivotal role in Zimbabwe's 99-run victory but also showcased a promising partnership with Craig Ervine, who contributed 93 runs. Zimbabwe's bowlers were equally impressive, dismissing Bangladesh for 172 runs, marking a historic day in Zimbabwean cricket.

title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
content: Egypt announced its willingness to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia to ensure its security and stability. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi convened the National Defence Council to discuss potential support amid Houthi assaults. These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited.

title: Taylor Swift’s $50,000 gift still supports Seattle Symphony school programme
content: In December 2015, Taylor Swift made a notable donation of $50,000 to the Seattle Symphony. This contribution supported the Link Up education programme, which introduces orchestral music to young students. The funding also benefitted the musicians' pension fund as part of the symphony's broader mission. Over the years, Link Up has successfully engaged thousands of children through interactive music experiences.

title: Tony Bennett-backed New York arts school marks 25 years with major facilities
content: Tony Bennett and Susan Benedetto co-founded the Frank Sinatra School of the Arts in 2001 in New York. The school offers specialized training in various art forms while maintaining a strong academic curriculum. Students can major in dance, drama, film, fine art, vocal music, or instrumental music. The school moved to a permanent facility in 2009, equipped with state-of-the-art spaces for performance and production.

title: Google cofounder Sergey Brin donated $100 mn but cannot cast a vote next month
content: Sergey Brin has made a significant contribution against California's proposed billionaire wealth tax to avoid financial impacts. After relocating to Nevada, he is no longer eligible to vote on this measure. This one-time tax is set to apply only to California residents from 2026 if approved. Other tech billionaires like Eric Schmidt and Peter Thiel have joined Brin in opposing the tax.

title: Rescue Labrador becomes marine detection dog, wins 2026 Animal of the Year
content: Sgiath, a remarkable six-year-old black Labrador, has recently made headlines for her extraordinary ability to detect invasive sea squirt, leading her to win the prestigious 2026 Animal of the Year Award. Partnering with marine ecologist Dr. Texa Sim, Sgiath's keen sense of smell plays a vital role in identifying this invasive organism. Her early detection skills contribute significantly to marine conservation efforts.

title: 'BJP conspiring to add fake votes': Akhilesh makes big claim, questions need for SSR
content: Akhilesh Yadav has accused the BJP of manipulating electoral rolls by adding fake votes and deleting genuine votes. He urged party workers to remain vigilant at polling booths and defend against electoral malpractice. Yadav raised concerns over the Election Commission's rationale for revising electoral rolls, questioning the need for it. He also criticized the BJP government's performance on various issues impacting citizens, including education and corruption.

title: Google Maps route likely led truck to Gwalior temple: Police
content: Around 1.30 am on Sunday, a heavy truck collided with devotees at Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior. The tragic incident resulted in at least 16 fatalities and numerous injuries among attendees. Authorities are investigating how the truck bypassed vehicle restrictions near the temple during the festival. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed distress, offering condolences and financial support for the victims’ families.

title: JD Vance’s immigration tiger is turning on its rider
content: US Vice President JD Vance admitted his rhetoric on H-1B visas was flawed during a recent town hall event. An Indian-American woman challenged him on his stance, suggesting it scapegoats immigrants. Vance defended his position by claiming he was criticizing corporate practices rather than foreign workers. His remarks have led to significant backlash from various groups regarding his mixed heritage.

title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions
content: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf raise $300,000 for charity with 20 luxury watches
content: In 2018, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf celebrated their partnership with Longines by organizing a charity auction. The auction raised $300,000 for their respective foundations, supporting education and children's trauma recovery. The event took place at the Musée Rodin in Paris, highlighting their decade-long collaboration with the watchmaker. Graf's foundation, Children for Tomorrow, expanded its reach into schools thanks to newfound funding.

title: How Tom Brady's childhood love for baseball cards inspired his business
content: Tom Brady's love for baseball cards began in his youth and has only deepened over the years. His treasured collection of Don Mattingly cards symbolizes his lifelong enthusiasm. Now, as a co-owner of CardVault, he is dedicated to enhancing the store's impact in the trading card world. Brady aims to enrich inventory and elevate customer experiences, striving to motivate a fresh wave of collectors through his entrepreneurial ventures.

title: Gwalior temple tragedy: CM Yadav orders City SP’s removal, 8 others after 14 deaths

A truck incident at Sheetla Mata temple resulted in 14 deaths and 28 injuries, prompting immediate action. Compensation of Rs 4 lakh has been announced for the families of the deceased. The chief minister stated that a detailed investigation would be initiated to identify responsible parties.

title: ‘With help of God & your prayers’: Pope makes first public appearance after surgery
content: Pope Leo XIV recently made his first public appearance following surgery for lung cancer. He expressed gratitude for the prayers and support he received during his recovery. The pontiff confirmed that he will gradually return to his duties with continued prayer and divine assistance. His next major engagement is planned for November, which includes an overseas trip to South America.

title: FMCG firms feel the pinch: Will your favourite products cost more this Diwali?
content: FMCG companies face a challenging landscape as they contend with surging costs for essential raw materials like palm oil and sugar. The pressure on operating margins is significant and unlikely to alleviate soon. To maintain goodwill during the festive season, firms are absorbing some of these cost hikes rather than passing them on to consumers.

title: Woman locks herself in room with 2 children, attacks them with scissors; all 3 die
content: In Dantiya village, Usha Sharma fatally attacked her minor children following a family argument. After the incident, she also inflicted injuries on herself. Villagers heard screams and found the three individuals injured in a locked room. Despite being rushed to the hospital, the children and Usha were all pronounced dead. Usha's sister, who was present, sustained serious injuries and was taken for further medical care.

title: Sugar-free ethanol? Oil companies change recipe, here's what's next
content: The government's recent decision to exclude sugar-based raw materials from its ethanol procurement process marks a strategic shift aimed at boosting domestic sugar availability. By allowing oil marketing companies to source ethanol from grains and C-heavy molasses, the government addresses rising sugar prices linked to adverse weather. This procurement adjustment seeks to maintain the ethanol blending program while balancing local consumption and reducing reliance on oil imports.

title: 'Drishyam 3' BO Day 17: Film eyes Rs 350 crore domestic net on third Sunday
content: ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’, starring Ajay Devgn, continues its theatrical run in its third week. After earning Rs. 245.50 crore net in its opening week and adding Rs. 87.50 crore in week two, the crime thriller has taken its India net collection past Rs. 341 crore, according to Sacnilk’s latest available figures. The film’s worldwide gross has reached Rs. 528.77 crore. As Day 17 live tracking continues, the next major domestic target is the Rs. 350 crore India net mark.

title: ‘Lifetime subscription to pressure’: Ex-cricketer’s blunt defence of Sanju Samson
content: Aakash Chopra has raised concerns about Sanju Samson's continued exclusion from the ODI squad. Despite impressive ODI statistics, Samson was overlooked for the New Zealand series. Chopra highlighted that multiple other wicketkeeper-batters were not selected either, indicating a possible decision on Samson's future. He compared performance metrics between Samson and other T20I players to support his point. This scrutiny comes as discussions around Samson's place in the team continue.

Sahu's unsupported claims of illegal assets compel the formation of a Special Investigation Team. Arya highlights the vital role of women in speaking against domestic abuse, promoting empowerment and transparency amidst the tumult.

title: Holy cow! Rs 20 lakh paid for a cowshed that doesn’t exist

Despite receiving over Rs 20 lakh, the project features only a partially built boundary wall. Investigators revealed that the tender process was allegedly manipulated to benefit a specific supplier, resulting in legal action against six individuals. The Economic Offences Wing is actively investigating the irregularities surrounding the project's funding and execution.

title: 'It's murder': Big twist in Noida family deaths as dispute over property emerges

Relatives have accused family members of involvement in a property dispute, which may have led to distress. Neighbors reported frequent arguments within the household before the tragic incident.

title: Driver, owner arrested after truck rams devotees near Gwalior temple; 15 killed

title: France's 140 year old Town Hall survived World Wars but succumbed to protesters
content: 143-year-old town hall in the city of Limoges gutted in fire during violent protests in france . local officials said around two-thirds of the historic building had been destroyed in the fire . demonstrations over rising fuel prices, inflation and deteriorating public services turned violent in several cities . an estimated 550,000 people took part in the marches, the interior ministry says .
